question.prompt: The source requires the storefront discovery experience to "work on a phone" but does not define the observable pass condition to prove that for browsing and price discovery.

options.label: Define responsive browsing
options.detail: Treat the promise as satisfied when a visitor can view catalogue listings and their prices on a phone-sized browser without layout breakage that blocks use.

options.label: Define exact viewport
options.detail: Provide a specific phone viewport or device model that the phone-support promise must pass on.

options.label: Limit to smoke access
options.detail: Treat the promise as only requiring that the catalogue opens on a phone, without a stronger usability expectation.

content.risk_rationale: Most customers are expected to arrive on phones, so an undefined phone oracle could leave the highest-reach part of the storefront under-specified.

question.prompt: The source identifies a website storefront but does not provide the web entry URL needed to run browser tests for this use case.

options.label: Use variable
options.detail: Author later tests with a placeholder start URL variable such as {{start_url}} until the environment supplies the actual address.

options.label: Provide actual URL
options.detail: Supply the exact storefront URL for this test environment.

options.label: Provide route only
options.detail: Supply a stable path such as /shop and keep the domain environment-specific.

content.risk_rationale: Without a start URL the final browser tests will be unrunnable, but the functional AC design can still proceed using a placeholder.

content.text: A visitor can view bouquet listings in the bouquet catalogue.

expected_answer.operand: a bouquet listing is visible in the bouquet catalogue to a visitor

content.text: Every bouquet shown in the catalogue displays its price before any add-to-basket action.

expected_answer.operand: each bouquet shown in the catalogue has a visible price before any add-to-basket action

content.text: The storefront discovery experience works on a phone.

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied user-reach because price visibility affects every visitor's ability to assess products before ordering; money, auth, data-loss, and change-frequency were not evidenced for this browse-only promise.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the source states that most customers arrive on phones, making phone usability a broad customer-impact promise; money, auth, data-loss, and change-frequency were not evidenced here.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because access to catalogue listings is the entry point for all storefront discovery; money, auth, data-loss, and change-frequency were not evidenced for this promise.
